language_target: TraceQL as shipped in Tempo v3.0.2
method: black-box: every probe replayed against an unmodified grafana/tempo:3.0.2 container; 2xx=accept, 400=reject. Where the reference answered 400 with a type error it echoed its own fully parenthesised parse, which is recorded verbatim in reference_parse and is what fixes the precedence table. No Tempo source was read.

divergence_classes.title: unary '!' binds looser than comparison
divergence_classes.reference: '!' is an operand-level unary: it binds tighter than every comparison operator and tighter than '+'/'-', but looser than '^' and '*'/'/'/'%'.
divergence_classes.pulsus: '!' negates a whole field primary, i.e. the entire comparison.

divergence_classes.title: colon-scoped intrinsic rejected as a comparison right-hand side
divergence_classes.reference: Every colon-scoped intrinsic is an ordinary operand and is legal on either side.
divergence_classes.pulsus: The right-hand-side field predicate recognises dotted attributes and bare intrinsics only.

divergence_classes.title: unary '-' rejected outside the right-hand side
divergence_classes.reference: Unary '-' is an operand-level unary, legal anywhere an operand is.
divergence_classes.pulsus: Accepted only when the right-hand side already begins an arithmetic operand.

divergence_classes.title: a literal is rejected at the comparison left-hand side
divergence_classes.reference: Both sides of a comparison are full field expressions, so a literal (or a literal-only comparison) is legal.
divergence_classes.pulsus: The left-hand side must begin with a field.

divergence_classes.title: a parenthesised expression is rejected at the comparison left-hand side
divergence_classes.reference: Parentheses are an operand, so '(.a) = 1' and '(.a + 1) = 2' are legal.
divergence_classes.pulsus: A parenthesised field expression may only be a whole boolean primary.

divergence_classes.title: chained comparison rejected
divergence_classes.reference: Comparison operators are left-associative binary operators and chain: 'a = b = c' parses as '(a = b) = c'.
divergence_classes.pulsus: A second comparison operator is a positioned grammar error.

divergence_classes.title: aggregate argument must be a bare field
divergence_classes.reference: An aggregate argument is a full field expression (arithmetic, unary, parentheses, any intrinsic).
divergence_classes.pulsus: Restricted to 'duration' or an attribute.
divergence_classes.wire_note: PARSE axis only. Stage C widened the argument to a field expression and ported the reference's rule 11, so all four probes agree here. On the WIRE (parse -> validate -> plan) three of them are still planner 400s where the reference answers 2xx: avg(span:childCount) and avg(trace:duration) have no numeric aggregation path, and avg(.a + 1) is a composite source. Only avg((.a)) reaches a 2xx, because parentheses group without surviving into the AST, so it IS avg(.a). See wire_baseline.json and PROVENANCE.md.

divergence_classes.title: '^' associativity
divergence_classes.reference: MEASURED: 2 ^ 3 ^ 2 = 64. GROUPING (separately established, issue #335 Stage B): RIGHT-associative — 2 ^ 3 ^ 2 equals 2 ^ 8 (64) and not 9 ^ 2 (512), where 9 and 8 are the reference folds of 2^3 and 3^2. The value 64 alone does NOT establish grouping: the reference reaches it by right grouping combined with an operand-swapping integer ^ (ledger traceql-pow-integer-operand-swap), two errors cancelling. An earlier reading of this row derived left-associativity from the value and was wrong.
divergence_classes.pulsus: right-associative: 2 ^ (3 ^ 2). GROUPING AGREES with the reference; the VALUE differs (512 vs 64) because PulsusDB computes lhs^rhs where the reference's integer path swaps operands — a ledgered deliberate divergence, not a grammar difference.

divergence_classes.title: unary '-' versus '^'
divergence_classes.reference: '^' binds tighter than unary '-': -2 ^ 2 = -4.
divergence_classes.pulsus: unary '-' binds tighter: (-2) ^ 2 = 4.

divergence_classes.title: '&&' versus '||' inside a spanset filter
divergence_classes.reference: one precedence level, left-associative: 'a || b && c' parses as '(a || b) && c'.
divergence_classes.pulsus: '&&' binds tighter than '||'.

divergence_classes.title: '&&' versus '||' between spansets
divergence_classes.reference: one precedence level, left-associative (established by result differential, not status).
divergence_classes.pulsus: '&&' binds tighter than '||'.

divergence_classes.title: bare / '!' / '= nil' attribute spellings conflated onto existence
divergence_classes.reference: distinct semantics per spelling, established by result differential: bare attribute = truthiness (matches only a == true, at every scope); '!' = boolean NOT (matches only a == false; an absent attribute never matches; a non-boolean value is an evaluation error); '!= nil' = presence; '= nil' = stable but inscrutable result sets matching no simple predicate (neither absence nor negated presence).
divergence_classes.pulsus: one node pair: bare and '!= nil' both parse to Exists and evaluate as presence; '!' and '= nil' both parse to Not(Exists) and evaluate as absence, with identical canonical text.

divergence_classes.title: 'unspecified' missing from the span-kind statics
divergence_classes.reference: 'unspecified' is the first member of the Kind enum and a `static` terminal of its own (expr.y:436), so it is a value wherever any other kind keyword is.
divergence_classes.pulsus: SpanKindValue enumerates five members; the bare identifier 'unspecified' is a positioned parse error in every operand and hint position.
divergence_classes.wire_note: PARSE axis closed, wire axis not. Stage D1 added the sixth SpanKindValue variant, so all five probes parse and validate. On the WIRE (parse -> validate -> plan) one of them is still a planner 400 where the reference answers 2xx: `{ .a = unspecified }` compares an ATTRIBUTE against a kind static, and traces/filter.rs's attribute predicate has arms for string, bool, number, duration and regex values but none for a kind or status keyword. That gap predates D13 (`{ .a = server }` has the same shape) and D13 is what made it reachable through a probe. The four kind-INTRINSIC and hint probes reach 2xx. See wire_baseline.json.

divergence_classes.title: 'minInt' / 'maxInt' statics missing
divergence_classes.reference: The `static` production resolves the bare identifiers minInt and maxInt to math.MinInt / math.MaxInt from the token alone, with no left context (expr.y:442-452); every other identifier is 'unknown identifier'.
divergence_classes.pulsus: No identifier resolves to a numeric static; both spellings are a positioned parse error.

divergence_classes.title: 'nil' legal only as an '='/'!=' operand on a bare field
divergence_classes.reference: Six dedicated productions (expr.y:408-413) make NIL an operand of '=' and '!=' against a whole fieldExpression on either side, and NIL = NIL / NIL != NIL fold to the boolean false.
divergence_classes.pulsus: 'nil' is recognised only as the right-hand side of '='/'!=' against a bare Field; every other position is a positioned parse error.

divergence_classes.title: spanset by() takes ONE field expression, not a comma list of fields
divergence_classes.reference: groupOperation is `BY OPEN_PARENS fieldExpression CLOSE_PARENS` (expr.y:177-179): exactly one operand, and that operand is a full field expression. There is no COMMA in the production and fieldExpression has none either.
divergence_classes.pulsus: A comma-separated list of bare Fields — wider in one direction (the list) and narrower in the other (no arithmetic, unary, parentheses or comparison operand).
divergence_classes.wire_note: PARSE axis closed, wire axis not. Stage D2 rewrote groupOperation in both directions: the comma list is gone (a reference parse error we accepted AND served, withdrawn and ledgered) and the single operand is a full field expression. All six probes agree on parse. On the WIRE (parse -> validate -> plan) four of them are still planner 400s where the reference answers 2xx: by(.b + .c), by(-.b), by(!.b) and by(.b = 1) are COMPOSITE keys, and a grouping key must resolve to one per-span value, so search_plan.rs refuses them with a clean 400 naming the rendered key rather than answering a silent flat 200. by((.b)) reaches 2xx because parentheses group without surviving into the AST, so it IS by(.b). See wire_baseline.json.

divergence_classes.title: compare()'s optional numeric arguments
divergence_classes.reference: Three arities (expr.y:324-326): compare(f), compare(f, topN) and compare(f, topN, start, end), defaulting 10, 0, 0.
divergence_classes.pulsus: All three arities parse; topN and the (start, end] selection window are honoured by the engine, not merely accepted (issue #460).

divergence_classes.title: negative aggregate / metrics thresholds
divergence_classes.reference: scalarExpression carries SUB INTEGER|FLOAT|DURATION (expr.y:290-292) and metricsFilter carries `metricsFilterOperation SUB …` (expr.y:353-355), so a threshold may be negative.
divergence_classes.pulsus: Both threshold positions take an unsigned literal only; the leading '-' is a positioned parse error.

divergence_classes.title: a parenthesised spanset PIPELINE is an operand everywhere a spanset expression is
divergence_classes.reference: wrappedSpansetPipeline is `'(' spansetPipeline ')'` (expr.y:162-163), an alternative of spansetPipelineExpression (expr.y:159) and therefore an operand of every structural and logical operator at that level, and a root form (expr.y:130).
divergence_classes.pulsus: Parentheses at the spanset level wrap a spanset EXPRESSION only; a '|' inside them is a positioned parse error.

divergence_classes.title: a parenthesised scalar expression at a scalar-filter operand
divergence_classes.reference: scalarExpression is self-parenthesising (expr.y:279), so `(count()) > 4` is the same shape as `count() > 4`.
divergence_classes.pulsus: A pipeline stage must begin with a stage keyword; '(' there is a positioned parse error.

divergence_classes.title: a metrics threshold after a second-stage function, and chains of them
divergence_classes.reference: metricsSecondStagePipeline is left-recursive over both `PIPE metricsSecondStage` and `metricsFilter` (expr.y:361-366), so filters and second-stage functions interleave freely.
divergence_classes.pulsus: At most one trailing threshold, and only directly after the first-stage function; anything further is trailing input.

divergence_classes.title: a second-stage function with no first-stage metrics aggregation
divergence_classes.reference: metricsSecondStagePipeline is reachable only from `spansetPipeline PIPE metricsAggregation metricsSecondStagePipeline` (expr.y:133), so topk/bottomk without a first stage is a parse error.
divergence_classes.pulsus: topk(n)/bottomk(n) parse as an ordinary pipeline stage anywhere after a '|'.
divergence_classes.wire_note: PARSE axis only. Our parser accepts `| topk(n)` / `| bottomk(n)` with no first-stage metrics aggregation, which the reference parse-rejects. On the WIRE (parse -> validate -> plan) the two axes AGREE: metrics_plan.rs and search_plan.rs both refuse a bare second stage, so every probe of this class is a 400 on both sides. The gap is the parser's alone; see wire_baseline.json.

divergence_classes.title: repeated root with() clauses
divergence_classes.reference: `root: root hints` (expr.y:134) is LEFT-RECURSIVE, so a root query may carry more than one with(...) clause. The clauses do NOT concatenate: the rule's action is `expr.withHints($2)` and withHints is `r.Hints = h`, a plain ASSIGNMENT (ast.go:112-115 @ v3.0.2), so the LAST clause wins; only a single clause's comma list (hintList, expr.y:379-382) accumulates. Every clause order is accepted 200 (measured), which is what this accept-surface class scores; the last-wins RESULT is a semantic fact, established from the rule above and pinned on our side by accept/hints_repeated.golden.
divergence_classes.pulsus: The root hint clause is parsed once; a second with(...) is trailing input.

divergence_classes.title: a pipeline may BEGIN with a stage that is not a spanset filter
divergence_classes.reference: spansetPipeline has four leading alternatives (expr.y:165-169) — spansetExpression, scalarFilter, groupOperation, selectOperation — and three of them are not `{ … }`.
divergence_classes.pulsus: A query must begin with a spanset filter or '('; a leading by()/select()/count() is a positioned parse error.

closed_meaning_probes.evidence: { .a = 2 ^ 3 ^ 2 && "x" }: reference folds to (.a = 64). GROUPING is established from three folds, not from that one value: 2 ^ 3 ^ 2 -> 64, 9 ^ 2 -> 512, 2 ^ 8 -> 64, where 9 and 8 are the reference folds of 2 ^ 3 and 3 ^ 2 -- so the three-term form is the RIGHT grouping. This row previously recorded ((2 ^ 3) ^ 2), derived from the value 64 alone, and was wrong: the reference reaches 64 by right grouping combined with an operand-swapping integer ^ (ledger traceql-pow-integer-operand-swap), two errors cancelling. Grouping agrees; the operator diverges deliberately, so the folded VALUE here is 512 for PulsusDB. This probe scores grouping only.
result differential: '{ .x="a" } || { .x="b" } && { .x="zzz" }' returns no trace, matching the parenthesised '(A || B) && C' and not 'A || (B && C)'
